title: Energy and Chemical Change
seo_title: SSS 2 Chemistry: Energy and Chemical Change Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_code: SSS 2 Chemistry: Energy and Chemical Change
standard_text: Energy changes in reactions related to bond energy; exothermic and endothermic reactions; heat of reaction the energy change; activation energy and the activated complex; potential energy diagrams; the effect of a catalyst. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): exothermic and endothermic reactions, energy profiles and catalysts, energy diagrams, calorimetry and enthalpy and energy in reactions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Exothermic: the energy change is negative. Endothermic: the energy change is positive.
key_sub: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for a reaction.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is absorbed to break bonds and released when new bonds form. If more energy is released than absorbed, the reaction is exothermic (the energy change is negative), such as combustion. If more is absorbed, it is endothermic (the energy change is positive), such as photosynthesis.

Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for a reaction to start. The activated complex is the unstable, high-energy arrangement of atoms at the top of the energy curve. A catalyst gives another pathway with a lower activation energy; it does not change the energy change.

Example

the energy change = −890 kJ·mol⁻¹. Exothermic or endothermic?

Sign of the energy change

Answer: exothermic

Example

Does a catalyst change the energy change?

It lowers only the hump.

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking breaking bonds releases energy.
  • Thinking a catalyst is used up.
  • Reading the energy change from the top of the curve instead of from the reactants to the products.

faq.a: Friction supplies the activation energy; after that the exothermic reaction supplies its own.

items.q: Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
c: so the molecules have the same mass
so the charges are all zero
atoms are neither created nor destroyed, so each element must have the same number on both sides
to show the reaction is fast
items.e: Change only the coefficients, never the formulae.

items.q: CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O → CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): C=O = 799, O–H = 463, C–H = 413, O=O = 498. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 3,450 − 2,648 = +802 kJ.

items.q: What does the law of conservation of mass state?
c: mass is not created or destroyed in a chemical reaction
mass always increases in a reaction
products are always heavier than reactants
items.e: Atoms are rearranged, not lost.

items.q: 2NH<sub>3</sub> → N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): N–H = 391, N≡N = 945, H–H = 436. How much energy is released when the product bonds form?
CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O → CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): C=O = 799, O–H = 463, C–H = 413, O=O = 498. How much energy is released when the product bonds form?
What is the empirical formula of a compound?
c: the actual number of atoms in a molecule
the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element
items.e: Glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ has the empirical formula CH₂O.

items.q: 2H<sub>2</sub>O → 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): O–H = 463, H–H = 436, O=O = 498. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 1852 − 1,370 = +482 kJ.

items.q: Why is bond breaking endothermic?
c: bonds release energy when they break
energy is needed to overcome the attraction between the atoms

items.q: What is the molar volume of a gas at 25 °C and 100 kPa (SLC)?
items.e: At SLC 1 mol of any gas occupies 24.8 L.

items.q: What is an exothermic reaction?

one that releases energy to the surroundings, so the energy change is negative

items.q: Which energy unit is used for enthalpy changes of reactions?

items.q: How does a catalyst increase the rate of reaction?
c: it provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
it is used up in the reaction
it gives particles more kinetic energy
items.e: The catalyst is unchanged at the end.

items.q: What happens to the rate of a gas reaction if the pressure is doubled?
c: it increases, because the particles are closer together
items.e: Higher pressure means higher concentration of gas.

items.q: Increasing the concentration of a reactant…
c: increases the rate because collisions are more frequent
items.e: More particles in the same volume.

items.q: What happens to the activation energy when a catalyst is added?
c: a different route with a lower activation energy is used
it stays the same but molecules move faster
items.e: The original route is still there; the catalysed route is easier.

items.q: A catalyst is added to C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (hydrating ethene) at equilibrium. What happens?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right
the position of equilibrium does not change; equilibrium is reached faster
the equilibrium shifts to the left
items.e: A catalyst speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally.

items.q: Why does a small rise in temperature greatly increase the rate?
c: many more molecules have energy greater than the activation energy
items.e: The tail of the distribution beyond E<sub>a</sub> grows a lot.

items.q: A catalyst is added to N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub> (the Haber process) at equilibrium. What happens?

items.q: What is Le Chatelier's principle?
c: equilibrium always lies to the right
pressure has no effect on gases
a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in conditions
items.e: Use it to predict the effect of changing temperature, pressure or concentration.

items.q: How can the rate of the reaction between magnesium and acid be measured?

measure the pH once at the end

items.q: What does a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution show?

the number of collisions per second
the number of particles with each kinetic energy at one temperature
items.e: The area under the curve is the total number of particles.

items.q: What is the mode of a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution?
c: the most probable energy, at the peak
items.e: The mean energy is a little to the right of the peak.

items.q: A catalyst is added to CO + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> (the water–gas shift reaction) at equilibrium. What happens?

items.q: Where does the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve start?

items.q: On a Maxwell–Boltzmann diagram, how does a catalyst change the picture?
